ai.description: This slender snake reaches 60–90 cm. It is olive-brown with a distinct yellow or cream lateral stripe and a keeled dorsal scale texture. A dark streak typically extends from the eye to the jaw.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Olive Keelback is best distinguished by the prominent, pale yellow or cream-colored stripe running along the side of its head and neck, which lacks the dark borders found in similar species.
ai.habitat: *Atretium schistosum* inhabits freshwater bodies like ponds, marshes, and rice paddies in the Indian subcontinent, typically at low to moderate altitudes below 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Olive Keelback is primarily diurnal and hunts by actively foraging for frogs and tadpoles in shallow water or along the banks of streams and marshes.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Atretium schistosum* is oviparous, breeding primarily during the monsoon season. Females lay clutches of 12–30 eggs in burrows or under debris near water bodies.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Atretium schistosum* is found across peninsular India, primarily in the plains and low-elevation wetlands of the Western Ghats, Deccan Plateau, and eastern coastal regions.
